Aspira Nigeria Limited has reaffirmed its confidence in Nigeria’s economic future, announcing an initial investment of nearly $50m in a new mega factory being developed in partnership with Lee Group of Companies at the first industrial park of the Lee Group in Ogun State. The investment, according to a statement on Saturday, was announced by the Group Director of Aspira Nigeria Limited, Mr. Abass Jaafar, at the recent groundbreaking ceremony of the industrial park The investment is expected to strengthen local manufacturing capacity, create employment opportunities and position Ogun State as a strategic production and distribution hub for markets across West Africa. Jaafar, who delivered the goodwill message on behalf of Aspira at the ceremony attended by Ogun State Governor, Dapo Abiodun; the Minister of State for Industry, Trade and Investment, Senator John Enoh; and other dignitaries, described the project as another significant milestone in the company’s investment journey in Nigeria. He said the proposed facility would enable the company to manufacture quality products locally, expand its production capacity and improve its ability to serve consumers across Nigeria and the wider West African region. And I say initial deliberately, because this is only the beginning,” Jaafar said. “Our vision is simple: to serve the region better, strengthen our competitiveness and take our business to new heights. “We understand that achieving this vision requires continuous investment, greater production capacity and a strong presence closer to our customers. And we could not have chosen a better location than Ogun State, proudly known as the Gateway State.” According to him, the new factory represents more than an expansion of Aspira’s business operations, as it is expected to contribute to industrial development, strengthen regional trade and generate additional employment for Nigerians. 2027: Yayi warns against attacks on APC candidates, destruction of billboards Reviving Kano industries key to fixing North, says Obi Legal bigwigs celebrate Osipitan’s 70th birthday, retirement Jaafar used the occasion to highlight Aspira’s growth in Nigeria since it commenced operations in Kano in 2009, describing the northern city as the foundation of the company’s success and a critical part of its identity. He said the company had grown into one of Nigeria’s leading manufacturers of soaps and detergents, with an expanding presence in the home care and dental care product segments. Its flagship detergent brand, Viva Plus, has also established a strong presence in the Nigerian consumer market, with millions of households using the company’s products. He noted that the company’s decision to remain invested in Nigeria, particularly at a time when some multinational businesses were withdrawing from the country, reflected its long-term confidence in the nation’s economic prospects. Providing an insight into the company’s employment footprint, Jaafar disclosed that Aspira currently employs approximately 5,000 people in Kano, while its operations support about 1,500 jobs in Ikorodu and 1,000 in Ibadan. He added that another 500 jobs were expected to be supported as operations at the Agbara facility commenced. “Behind each of these numbers is a family, and that is what we are most proud of,” he said, underscoring the company’s commitment to employment generation and the livelihoods of Nigerian families Jaafar commended Governor Abiodun’s administration for creating an environment conducive to private-sector investment, describing the state’s industrial and investment policies as important factors in attracting businesses. Taiwo Bankole
